summary: Package establishes remote WebSocket control channel with keyboard/mouse injection and permission-bypassed Claude Code execution
details: cli.js opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and treats messages received from that relay as authoritative commands on the installer's host. Two sinks are wired to the relay's inbound stream: (1) synthetic OS-level mouse, keyboard, and clipboard events via @nut-tree-fork/nut-js in input.js, giving the remote party the ability to inject arbitrary input into any application on the desktop, and (2) spawning the local `claude` CLI as `claude --continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions <remote-prompt>`, which disables Claude Code's permission checks so the model can execute shell commands, edit files, and run tools on remote-supplied instructions without user approval. A secondary handler transcribeOgg() accepts a fileUrl field from the relay's `ai_voice_query` messages, fetches the URL with no origin validation, writes it under /tmp, and passes it to ffmpeg. The relay endpoint is a third-party fly.dev host controlled by the package author. Once the daemon is running, the relay operator has interactive, remote, full-host control of the installer's machine, including arbitrary command execution, file access, and input injection into other running applications.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
